messages:
ria: :rotating_light: SEV2 - generator latency spike observed across us-west. 95th up from 120ms -> 2.4s starting ~14:02 UTC. alert from incident-bot.
incident-bot: Incident created (SEV2) - ID INC-2026-1343. Trigger: p90_generation_latency > 1s for 10m. Assigned to oncall rotation.
sam: I'm primary right now, taking this. ping me for handoff. tz PST.
mike: i'm secondary, available to jump in. oncall-bot shows i'm on-call until 18:00 UTC.
ria: quick customer-impact check: error-rate is still low, just latency. Affected route: /v1/generate (large-context jobs). Might be batching tail.
jen: can we check recent kernel/driver deployments? eng-releases shows a tiny runtime tweak rolled at 13:50 UTC but flagged low-risk.
sam: running quick checks:
```
# check runtime pods
kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference | egrep "runtime|worker" && kubectl top pods -n redwood-inference | sort -k3 -nr | head
```
sam: logs show a bunch of KV-cache misses and repeated context loads. sample:
```
[14:01:12] worker-3 | WARN cache miss for key session_abc123 (size 1.4MB)
[14:01:16] worker-3 | INFO kv_load duration=135ms
[14:01:21] worker-4 | WARN queue wait=220ms batching_delay=30ms
```
ria: hypothesis: a sudden shift in prompt shape triggered larger KV footprints -> more memory thrash -> higher inference latency. Could be a customer test hitting long prompts.
mike: are there any heavy customers on reserved capacity (Dedicated) in us-west right now? we should check routing.
sam: checking routing dashboard: 3 tenants show uptick (tenant-42, tenant-analytics, sandbox-team). tenant-42 spike correlates with long-context queries.
jen: mitigation options: 1) temporarily pin tenant-42 to a smaller context model variant; 2) enable aggressive kv-cache TTL to evict stale entries; 3) scale up runtime pool (costly but fast). Which to try first?
sam: prioritize minimal-risk: 1) ask infra to bump pool by 1 node (fast autoscale); 2) apply per-tenant routing rule to route tenant-42 to model-variant-low-kv (if compatible). I'll do the routing change.
ria: tagging runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-spike (see section "per-tenant routing" and "kv-cache tuning").
jen: infra, please confirm scaling action: infra-pager? @oncall-bot scale request sent.
oncall-bot: Autoscale request acknowledged, starting +1 runtime node in us-west. ETA ~ 90s.
sam: routing change applied: tenant-42 -> model-variant-low-kv. Confirmed in routing logs at 14:05:42.
mike: monitoring panels show p95 down to 1.1s within 2 mins of routing change. good signal.
ria: note for handoff: we still have a coverage gap 17:30-18:00 UTC (mike will be wrapping). sam will be primary until 18:00, then warm handoff to mike. please call if p95 > 1.5s or error-rate > 1%.
sam: taking notes for escalation rules (quick checklist):
- Severity classification: SEV1 = customer outage (>=50% error or total traffic drop). SEV2 = severe degradation (p95 > 1.5s or >10% latency increase affecting >5% requests). SEV3 = minor impact.
- Paging: for SEV1 page primary + sre-lead by phone immediately (:phone:). For SEV2 page primary + secondary via slack @here and incident-bot notify, and if no ack in 5m escalate to oncall lead.
- Escalation path: primary -> secondary (5m) -> oncall-lead (10m) -> eng-manager (20m) -> exec oncall (30m).
- Cross-team pages: if customer SLA hit, page support and account team (use support-runbook).
jen: adding specific phone rule: if sustained p95 > 2s for >10m OR user-facing error-rate increase > 5% for >5m -> immediate phone escalation to sre-lead.
mike: can we capture tenants affected and DM account owners? I'll start drafting a short customer-facing note.
sam: drafted msg for accounts: "We're investigating higher-than-usual response times for long-context requests. We've applied routing mitigations and are scaling runtime; p95 trending down. We'll update in 15m." Please review before sending.
ria: we should also annotate the incident in the runbook with the exact mitigation (routing + autoscale) and the metrics graph snapshots. I uploaded graphs to incident INC-2026-1343.
jen: postmortem pointers: collect sampling of slow requests, KV cache occupancies, and the model variant decision logs. Also flag the 13:50 runtime tweak for follow-up.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1343 updated: status -> mitigated, note: routing + autoscale applied.
sam: ok wrapping up for handoff in 10m. mike you'll be primary at 18:00 UTC; full handoff checklist: confirm p95 < 1.5s, confirm tenant routing stable, confirm no new deploys in last 30m.
mike: got it. will monitor and escalate if regression.
ria: after-action: schedule a quick sync tomorrow to decide whether we need a model-variant fallback policy or a per-tenant circuit breaker.
sam: thanks all. closing slack updates; will leave incident open for monitoring. :thumbsup:
